searchText: this has probably been addressed, but is there any reason why ethereum doesn't support self-executing contracts? ie. execute some function at block X, as long as contract has enough eth to pas for gas of course How do you decide what gas price to offer? There's a huge potential for DOS vectors there as well, or even just the burden of long ago forgotten contracts that continue firing off transactions that no one actually cares about. Paying gas provides some protection against this but it's quite expensive just to track whether a tx should be fired for all the contracts in the world state and gas is only paid when they actually trigger. good points. definitely don't want contracts spamming network, even if they have the ETH to pay for it. and yeah, i guess it becomes much more complex for EVM. it would have to keep a huge list of all contracts with automatic execution thank! Not really but kind of. Front ends usually take a high level language and translate it to an AST then IR , I’m interested in going from evm bytecode to a high level language. So reverse It’s not really the same as trying to recover contract code from bytecode , it’s more akin to transpiling bytecode compiled from Solidity to a different contract language <@823926145950548069> does this high level language has an optimizer? https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/745077610685661265/856606582015131659 continuing this here (cc <@!619138323776012307> <@!301186049323958275>) > that’s a thing. you cannot really. You still need to update your account. So I get why some empty blocks are actually not empty and full the whole space with gas token (account update for block reward + predefined state update for the whole gas token creation) Not sure what you mean by this, updating just the coinbase balance is only around a dozen hashes where an entire block could be many more. Miners are starting with "empty" blocks full of gas tokens now because they're also simple and quick to build > But I still don’t get if there are actual empty blocks in Eth like we have in Bitcoin do empty blocks in btc not pay out to the coinbase?

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: How do you decide what gas price to offer? There's a huge potential for DOS vectors there as well, or even just the burden of long ago forgotten contracts that continue firing off transactions that no one actually cares about. Paying gas provides some protection against this but it's quite expensive just to track whether a tx should be fired for all the contracts in the world state and gas is only paid when they actually trigger.
